title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. A is an abelian scheme over a base of characteristic p, presumably with ordinary fibres; the next page says 'si A connexe ...'. Write T_p(A)_ét for the Tate module of the étale part of A[p^∞]. A and its dual A^∨ have the same p-rank, so T_p(A)_ét and T_p(A^∨)_ét are free Z_p-modules (lisse Z_p-sheaves) of the same rank. Grothendieck wants a canonical isomorphism α_A : det T_p(A)_ét ≅ det T_p(A^∨)_ét, compatible with base change.

The construction:
1. Choose a polarization φ̃ : A → A^∨, coming from L with deg φ̃ = χ(L)^2.
2. φ̃ gives a map det T_p(φ̃)_ét between the two determinant lines. It is not an isomorphism: its image is p^v times a generator, where v = ν_p(card Coker T_p(φ̃)_ét).
3. Normalize by dividing by the canonical square root Δ(φ̃) of deg φ̃ (essentially χ(L)).
4. The previous page shows the result is independent of φ̃. Changing φ̃ by a Rosati-symmetric positive u multiplies by det T_p(u)_ét. Its square is deg u = Δ(u)^2. The sign is fixed because Δ(u) = Δ(w)^2 ≥ 0 on the positive cone, where u = w^2.
5. Point (b): the normalized map has unit determinant, i.e. ν_p(card Coker T_p(φ̃)_ét) = ν_p(√deg φ̃).

This page proves (b):
- By a snake-lemma argument on étale parts of p-divisible groups, Coker T_p(φ̃)_ét ≅ (Ker φ̃)(p)_ét.
- Ker φ̃ is self-dual (Cartier), via the Weil pairing e^φ̃.
- Cartier duality exchanges the étale part with the multiplicative ('rad') part. So the étale part of Ker φ̃(p) is dual to its multiplicative part, and the two have the same order.
- Since A is ordinary (reading 'comme A ordinaire'), Ker φ̃(p) = étale × multiplicative, with no local–local part. Hence (ord Ker φ̃(p)_ét)^2 = ord Ker φ̃(p) = (deg φ̃)(p), which gives the required valuation identity.

Conclusion, boxed (*): a canonical isomorphism α_A : det T_p(A)_ét ≅ det T_p(A^∨)_ét, compatible with base change and functorial for isomorphisms.

Corollary (bracketed): let u be an automorphism of A and ǔ = (u*)^{-1} its covariant action on A^∨. Transport by α gives det T_p(u)_ét = det T_p(ǔ)_ét = (det T_p(u*)_ét)^{-1}. Hence the boxed identity det T_p(u)_ét · det T_p(u*)_ét = 1.

Warning: for a mere endomorphism u, in general det T_p(u)_ét ≠ det T_p(u*)_ét. The next page says the product is a 'degré'.

The next page plans further checks: α_{A^∨} = α_A^{-1} up to sign, and α_A agrees with the isomorphism coming from duality in de Rham (unit-root) cohomology.

Purpose: make p-adic étale/unit-root determinant data of A and A^∨ canonically comparable. This serves the crystalline/Barsotti–Tate study of ordinary abelian schemes.
errors: The equality (ord Ker φ̃(p)_ét)^2 = ord Ker φ̃(p) holds only if Ker φ̃(p) has no local–local part. That is the ordinary case (the hard-to-read word is very likely 'ordinaire'). Without ordinarity it fails: for a supersingular elliptic curve and φ = λ∘[p], the left side is 1 and the right side is p^2. So the construction is valid only on the ordinary locus, or needs a different normalization (by the étale part of the kernel).
Self-duality of Ker φ̃ requires φ̃ to be a polarization (symmetric), not an arbitrary isogeny A → A^∨. This is implicit.
The final warning 'det T_p(u) ≠ det T_p(u*)' must refer to the étale parts. On the full Tate module/Dieudonné module both determinants equal deg u.
'(Ker φ̃(p))_rad': the Cartier dual of the étale part is the multiplicative part (radiciel with étale dual), not the whole radiciel part. This agrees only under ordinarity.

ideas.what: Coker of T_p(φ)_ét on étale Tate modules is identified with the étale part of the p-primary kernel of the isogeny
ideas.modern_name: snake lemma for isogenies of p-divisible groups / étale parts

ideas.what: Kernel of a polarization is Cartier self-dual, so its étale and multiplicative parts have equal order; for ordinary A the étale part's order is the square root of the p-part of the degree
ideas.modern_name: Weil pairing e^λ on ker λ; deg φ_L = χ(L)^2

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism det T_p(A)_ét ≅ det T_p(A^∨)_ét for ordinary abelian schemes, obtained from any polarization normalized by the sign-fixed square root χ(L) of its degree, and independent of the polarization
ideas.modern_name: canonical identification of determinants of the unit-root / étale parts of A[p^∞] and A^∨[p^∞]
ideas.usually_credited_to: no specific attribution known to me; related to the Serre–Tate/Katz theory of ordinary abelian varieties and unit-root crystals

ideas.what: For automorphisms u: det T_p(u)_ét · det T_p(u^∨)_ét = 1; fails for general endomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: compatibility of the étale determinant character with duality

missed.claim: Grothendieck plans to show that the étale determinant isomorphism α_A matches the duality isomorphism on de Rham/crystalline (unit-root) cohomology, and that α_{A^∨} = α_A^{-1} up to sign. These checks are left 'à vérifier'. A canonical integral comparison of determinants of unit-root parts for A and A^∨, normalized via χ(L), is not something I can locate stated in this form.
missed.quote: Cela définit bien un isomorphisme canonique det T_p(A)_ét ≅ det T_p(A^*)_ét compatible avec changement de base
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor but clean integral refinement relevant to unit-root F-crystals and p-adic determinant characters on the ordinary locus (Katz/Hida settings) when the polarization is not principal. Its value is mostly historical, showing Grothendieck working out the p-adic/crystalline side of duality in 1969.

deep.surprise_reason: The construction is careful: it normalizes by the Riemann–Roch square root χ(L) to make the isomorphism polarization-independent. But each step is standard, and the result is a modest refinement in ordinary p-divisible group theory. It is plausibly folklore and of limited consequence.
transcription_corrections: 'comme on a dimension[?]' should very likely read 'comme A ordinaire,' (the ordinarity hypothesis needed for the order computation).
'invariant[?] en A' is probably 'fonctoriel/compatible avec isomorphismes en A' (functorial for isomorphisms in A).
'Cokn T_p(φ̃)_ét ≃ (Ker T(φ̃))(p)_ét': the first line has a struck-through 'T' inside 'Ker'.
